item.title: A problem with alot of scp articles.
item.content:encoded:
Input: 1 chimp (setting: Fine)

Output: [DATA EXPUNGED]

Input: 1 chimp (setting: Rough)

Output: Badly mutilated corpse, showing signs of crushing and cutting with high heat

Those are lines from SCP-914. Why would the SCP use 'chimp' instead of chimpanzee?
A lot of SCPs are structured like poorly-written wikipedia articles, instead of actual scientific reports.
Censored information makes no sense either, why would it be censored in the first place?
Honestly, draft-reviewers should be more informed of things like this.

item.title: How did they contain SCP-106 before they had tech they do now?
item.content:encoded:
As some of you may know, the foundation was trying to contain SCP-106 (he was discovered by them) in the middle of WW2. How did they deal with him back then?

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

SCP-106 was around (known by the foundation) since the middle of WW2. Say what you want about advanced WW2 tech, they didn't have electromagnets capable of lifting a chamber the size of SCP-106's in the air 24/7. By the yes I am accounting for more advanced foundation tech, assuming the foundation gets access to experimental highly advanced tech the entire world helped make, in 1940 that would put their tech at the 1960's/70s. They couldn't have used modern SCP to contain him, so how did they?

item.title: I'd Rather Be Part of the Serpent's Hand Than the Foundation"
item.description: I would be going, "SCREW THE FOUNDATION, YO! DOWN WITH THOSE GOSHDARN JAILORS!"
item.content:encoded:
So, I think the Serpent's Hand would be better to be a part of / work for than the SCP Foundation. Here are all my points, in no particular order:

1. Foundation operates out of boringly-decorated, overly sanitary-looking research facilities filled with deadly monsters that can get loose at any second, not to mention they are constantly raided by the Chaos Insurgency. The Serpent's Hand gets a frikin' extradimensional library that requires actual frikin' magic to access, and is actually very safe because all of the anomalies within are friendly as long as nobody gets violent against them or breaks the rules. Nice place to chill and relax, maybe play some Dungeons and Dragons and write in peace.

2. Foundation deprives anomalous humans of their humanity, and instead locks them up in basically prison (I don't give a crap about how much you think Iris Thompson likes it there, she most likely secretly hates being locked up, along with literally any other human SCP).

3. They fight for the rights of law-abiding anomalous humans that just want to go about their lives without having to worry about being either imprisonated by the SCP Foundation, murdered by the Global Occult Coalition, weaponized by the Chaos Insurgency, or sold by MC&D. Basically, they tell everybody else to chill their heels and leave anomalous people the heck alone. Which is actually a pretty noble cause. The only reason they raid Foundation / GoC locations is because that is one of the only ways to get their points across. Plus, they do stealth missions, and kill Foundation personnel in only a limited capacity.

+ show block
– hide block

4. The Serpent's Hand doesn't breach dangerous anomalies for no good reason at all. That's the Chaos Insurgency's job, after all. If the Serpent's Hand doesn't have a good reason to breach any given SCP during a raid, they won't breach said SCP. They do, however, steal Safe SCP items, and let peaceful human SCPs to escape. They may even attempt to free D-class if possible. They're not stupid, and they don't want to bring about the end of the world by releasing highly dangerous Euclid, Keter, and Apollyon SCPs. Again, that is the Chaos Insurgency's job.

5. Simply existing as a worker on a Foundation site means that you are alive on moment, and then the next you are dead due to being freakin' eaten by a massive lizard that is literally too angry to die or turned into a zombie by a dude cosplaying as a medieval plague doctor, and your friends and family will be unaware of your death (if all of them are outside of the foundation, which is most likely). If you do manage to survive through the containment breach, you will still be mentally scarred by the experience. As I said earlier, the Serpent's Hand operates out of a peaceful library, with a 0% chance of being eaten by a bloodthirsty monster.

6. I also believe that the serpent's hand probably is one of the morally better GoIs, considering their entire mission statement is "we want rights for anomalous humans, and knowledge about the paranormal should be public." While they do break the law from time to time (which would make them Chaotic or Neutral Good), they don't do so for no reason at all. They just want the world to be a better place.

item.title: Foundation Governance
item.description: Some notes on real-world Foundation governance and Coups, as Canon Fodder
item.content:encoded:
+ show block
– hide block

In 2014 The Mastercoin Foundation had a board composed of 8 or 9 members, several of whom were friends or colleagues in a private venture fund of the director, who had replaced the first director, who had resigned out of a sense that there was no business model to the protocol we were building. A measure was proposed to the board that the Foundation purchase-back a large supply of the coin that was sold in the original fundraiser in 2013. The measure passed, but the parameters weren't specified. The director then conducted what the tax-code would call a "self-dealing" transaction where his private fund divested an illiquid position at a non-fair-market-value price. This effectively defunded all the remaining Bitcoin in the treasury, and everyone went on as volunteers for almost a year, sort of unaware of this. The one who was aware didn't know what to do about it, he informed me, I found something in the tax code severely penalizing this sort of thing, we got the money back.

The custody of the assets was a key point of failure. I did right by everyone but could have absconded with enough BTC to value it at about 18M USD today, whew. Instead we did payrolls and so on, and a year later made a major release.

The counter-coup the effectively oustered me had to do with custody of reserve assets. I was told I'd get back-filled on some expenses but this never happened. The board consisted of me, a young guy who had invested in the ICO, the original founder who had washed his hands, and this other guy who co-founded Tether. The original founder deferred his vote to the Tether guy, effectively turning the board into a null entity. Everything came down to keys.

Another coup that occurred in this time period, involving more money and a higher profile project, involved the Ethereum Foundation. Gavin Wood twisted Vitalik's arm to fire Charles Hoskinson as CEO, Charles was trying to get them 100M in funding at a 1B valuation from Google Ventures. Gavin said he and other core devs would walk if Vitalik didn't fire Charles. So in this case the coup was less mechanical and more an emotional manipulation of a young and inexperience de facto controller.

The Foundation in this verse has much better governance than these real-world, shabby examples. Actual Private Foundations that are 501(c)3 accredited by the IRS have strict guidelines about what can be done with the money and how much should be spent per year on the mission (5%). You can give you niece a job that she legitimately does but you can't have the foundation pay you rent for a property you own.

In the Foundation-verse, the Foundation may well be a registered 501(c)3 entity with 995 return going back to the 70s, hiding in plain sight on government databases. Its governance has been a subject of a lot of eerie conspiracy theories. Sometimes, such as in the SCP-001 proposal where the SCP is the former O-13, the violent coup is due to anomalous effects. Sometimes, such as the 001 proposal masterwork involving the Chaos Insurgency dossier on the original council, it's the other way around. I think you could imagine a headcanon where both SCP files are sort-of true but also perhaps laden with disinfo.

I think the best effects are when the governance seems very competent, the Ethics Committee seems to be doing its best to keep things measured, there is some tension/uncertainty about one vs. the other. The idea that the O5 Council is not unilaterally powerful is interesting. The EC being a vector of infiltration is interesting. O5's being afflicted with antimemetic blindspots could be somewhat interesting if couched properly.

I think the big lesson though, to take from these tales of Crypto-Coups, is that *key custody is everything*. A charter is, to paraphrase George W Bush, just a piece of paper. The design of the charter could be mildly interesting to explore. Some infohazard contamination adjusting it might be interesting. But who has custodial control, and is therefore entrusted, with the "assets" of the Foundation, which are not magical internet monies but rather, presumably, key Thaumiel objects and entities.

Also, 4800 is a great pataphysical SCP, where Scranton's inventions and the Thaumiel class are anomalous. Things can definitely be done with this.

The question of turn-over on the O5 Council is interesting to explore. If both 001 proposals regarding the council are both somewhat true +/- disinfo cover, it's possible there was an original set of O5's who were killed and the turnover is part of the meta-process of the Foundation's governance, which may itself be anomalous. I had an idea for an esoteric Thaumiel regarding the principles governing the EC, but it's going to take a lot of revision and I imagine, collab. on mythos implications.

If humanoids are high difficulty, Thaumiel's higher, Thaumiel humanoids even higher, then combining these with O5/EC intrigue may be the highest-difficulty tales/SCPs to do well.

It's worth noting that by 2018 the crypto "industry" generally pivoted from foundations to private companies, from public funding with a sense of social contract, to private funding from angels/VCs, because of how faulty the idealistic conception of an honest foundation proved to be in practice.

Yet in the Foundation-verse, there is the sort of problem that only minimizes downside out of a sense of duty, without much profit motive, which fits a Foundation perfectly. There are a lot of moments where you can really think, wow the governance is on-point, O5's are super careful and the EC keeps things from being cruel. Subverting that in fridge logic ways can be a great payoff.

item.title: Earth's Increasing Mass
item.description: Lots of SCPs (646, 871, 1680), create a constant stream of mass from nowhere. Is that a problem?
item.content:encoded: I am wondering if the Foundation has any plan for dealing with all the excess mass that results from these SCPs. They've found short-term ways to keep the Keter cakes from overrunning the planet, but the mass of the consumed cakes is still conserved by D-class digestion. The same goes for 646's terminated offspring and 1680's clones of Tyler Buchanan used as D-class. The mass of the SCP-verse's planet Earth is gradually increasing and, without some way to destroy all that mass or send it somewhere else, will continue to do so. Are there other anomalies that are constantly destroying mass and therefore balancing this somewhat? Or is the increase so small that it simply won't matter against the mass of the entire planet?

item.title: A question about the Anomalous Intelligence Community
item.description: Or, "Does the UIU have a rival?"
item.content:encoded:
Not in the sense of groups like the GOC, Foundation and so on and so forth where the Unusual Incidents Unit calling them their 'rivals' would be paying themselves a pretty generous compliment, but instead I mean… well, doing a dive into the UIU hub it occurred to me that the FBI is largely limited in scope to inside of the United States.

Which is all well and good… but, the United States has interests outside of its own borders.

The CIA, conversely, operates mostly abroad as a covert agency.

So, my question is: Does the CIA have its own equivalent to the UIU, or would they borrow a 'specialist' from them in the event they have to deal with something anomalous? Or do they simply hand it off to the Foundation, or the GOC or someone similar?

Has this been addressed in a tale or on one of the hubs?
